sections.title: The standard way
sections.body: Cho hỏi, đi tới đó thế nào? is the safest default for "Excuse me, how do I get there?". Use this when you need the route to a place and can point or name it separately. Say it slowly, then point, show your phone, or hold up the item if the other person needs more context.

sections.title: Why it matters
sections.body: Direction phrases turn a vague travel problem into a specific next step.

sections.title: When to use it
sections.body: Use this when you need the route to a place and can point or name it separately. Use it in finding places, turns, distance, and walking directions when one clear sentence will work better than a long explanation.

sections.title: Watch out
sections.body: If the answer is long, ask them to point or type it. Street directions can be hard to catch by ear.

sections.title: Local tip
sections.body: Show the map or address first, then ask the phrase. The answer is easier to understand when both of you see the same place.
